newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Great River sets minimum '96 profit.
newsitem.headline: Great River sets minimum '96 profit.

text.p: Indonesia's largest fashion retailing company PT Great River Industries is targeting a minimum net profit of 26 billion rupiah for fiscal year ending December 1996, said president director Sunjoto Tanudjaja on Tuesday.
"Great River targets a minimum profit of 26 billion rupiah by the end of this year," Tanudjaja told a news conference.
The company is targeting sales of 254 billion rupiah for the same period, he said, up from 182.3 billion rupiah in 1995.
"We have identified Asia Pacific and ASEAN as strong growth regions for the company," he added.
ASEAN comprises Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Philippines, Indonesia, Brunei and Vietnam.
He said the company would grow through strategic alliances with the world's leading textile and garment manufacturers.
Great River would continue to gain access to export markets in the Asia Pacific and increase production efficiency.
The company would substitute locally produced raw materials for those previously imported to lower overall costs.
He saw future growth in the Indonesian market after the phasing out of duties among ASEAN countries in 2003 with AFTA (ASEAN Free Trade Area).
Tanudjaja saw the home market customer base growing from 200 million currently to about 350 million by 2003.
